lesson_title: Perimeter, Area and Material Costs: Pricing a Real Yard
hook_text: You measured the yard at 41 metres of fence. You just wasted R867. Here's why.
clip_script: Yard: 12,5 metres by 8. Walk it — 12,5 plus 8 plus 12,5 plus 8 is 41 metres. So order 41 metres of fencing, right? No. There's a 3 metre gate in that line, and the gate comes from a different shelf. Fencing is 38 metres. At R289 a metre that's R10 982 — and if you'd ordered 41 you'd have thrown away R867 on fence that must stand where the gate opens. Now the walls. Room is 4,2 by 3,6, walls 2,5 high. Walk the floor's edge — 15,6 metres — times the height, 2,5. That's 39 square metres of wall. Take off the door, 1,8. Take off the window, 1,8. Thirty-five point four to paint. But the tin says TWO coats — so you're really covering 70,8. Paint does 8 square metres a litre, so 8,85 litres. Walk into the shop and ask for 8,85 litres. They'll look at you. You buy two 5-litre tins. R1 050. Always round UP — running short stops the job.
visual_style: Tape measure snapping around a real township yard, the gate section flashing red as it is removed from the count; walls unrolling into one long rectangle; paint tins stacking with the fractional litre crossed out.
mood: Hands-on, practical, the confidence of someone who has priced a job before.
pacing: Quick around the fence, a hard stop on the gate, steady through the wall arithmetic, punchy at the shop counter.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and price any building job to the last rand.
